result.title: What have we learned from the Strait of Hormuz closure?
result.description:
‘We've really learned about asymmetry, haven't we?’

Adam Tooze, Director of the European Institute at Columbia University, discusses with the World Economic Forum’s Robin Pomeroy the impact of the Strait of Hormuz closure - and what it might mean for green technology.

Adam Tooze was a guest on our #RadioDavos podcast.

result.title: Ideas On The Move: Shoukei Matsumoto
result.description:
‘As long as we are staying in the optimizing mindset, we are living in the past.’

For Buddhist monk Shoukei Matsumoto, the question isn’t how to leave a great legacy – but what not to leave behind. Guided by a Buddhist view of ancestry, he believes becoming a good ancestor is about subtracting rather than adding.

It’s a mindset that has taken him from studying literature at Tokyo University to learning at a temple and then an MBA.

He joined us for #IdeasOnTheMove at #AMGFL26 in Dubai to share why we need to break out of existing frames of thinking.

result.title: Ideas On The Move: Jared Genser
result.description:
‘There is extraordinary promise in emerging neurotechnologies, especially to cure brain diseases.’

But international human rights lawyer Jared Genser warns that as wearable brain devices go global, they put our privacy, agency and identity at risk.

Driven by a relentless pursuit of justice, he joined us in Dubai at #AMGFL26 to explain why protecting the human mind is the most urgent human rights frontier.

result.title: Ideas On The Move: Alicia Chong Rodriguez
result.description:
‘#AI can include women but also still learn to ignore them.’

Engineer and inventor Alicia Chong Rodriguez is on a mission to close the diagnostic blind spots in women’s #cardiovascular health.

That’s why she started Bloomer Tech: to collect life-saving data on heart disease in women, which is frequently misdiagnosed and under-researched.

She joined us at #AMGFL26 in #Dubai to share how her company is transforming everyday bras into smart medical devices to tackle this issue.

result.title: The Supermarket Fridge Hack & The Race For Critical Minerals | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - French supermarket fridges hacked:
Hackers overrode the temperature settings at hundreds of stores across France, heating fridges as high as 50°C and spoiling millions of euros’ worth of food. The event has laid bare how much #cyberattacks can impact everyday life, says Akshay Joshi, the Forum’s Head of Cybersecurity.

03:10 - Critical minerals race enters new phase:
The race for critical minerals is entering a new phase as demand surges from #AI, electrification and the wider #energy transition. Here, Yun B. Choi, CEO and Executive Chairman of Korea Zinc, explains why building resilient, diversified processing capacity is becoming a strategic priority.

05:07 - Can micro-enterprise beat poverty?:
The solution to poverty isn’t handing out aid, says this social entrepreneur - it lies in creating new markets that serve those most in need. Jacqueline Novogratz, founder of non-profit impact investment platform Acumen Fund, has spent more than two decades investing in #entrepreneurs whose work helps lift people out of poverty.

08:50 - Why cybersecurity needs new a approach:
As #AI increases in power and scale, so do the opportunities for those who would use it as a weapon or tool for criminality.  The global response to these threats is not yet up to speed, argues Kat Duffy, Senior Fellow for Digital and Cyberspace Policy at the Council On Foreign Relations.
